title: Buck Rogers: Countdown to Doomsday
container: DAX (little-endian, signed-byte RLE) + FBOV overlay pool

files.label: TITLE (title screen)
files.note: 4 chunky-item frames. The install is VGA, not EGA: BUCK.CFG's first field is V where Champions' and Death Knights' KRYNN.CFG/DKK.CFG hold E in the identical field position, and the picture blocks carry their own 224-entry 6-bit DAC palettes.

files.label: PIC1 (animated scenes)
files.note: VGA compressed picture, 3 blocks / 11 frames of 88x88. Across pic1..pic9 the family is 40 blocks / 88 frames; 12 of those blocks are multi-cel animations of 3, 3, 3, 4, 4, 4, 4, 6, 6, 6, 8 and 9 frames.

files.label: 8X8D1 (8x8 tile sheet)
files.note: 2 tile sheets plus block #201, a text font: 2048 bytes of 1bpp 8x8 glyphs (256 slots, MSB first), addressed by the SAME `ToUpper(ch) % 64` fold as CoK/DoK's own COK_FONT_BLOCK (loaders/cokFont.ts), not a linear count from '@'. Under that fold, digits and punctuation ARE present ('0' is slot 48, populated) -- an earlier reading of this note counted linearly from '@' and concluded they were missing, which the arithmetic itself rules out (code - 0x40 is negative for every digit). 70 of the 256 slots are populated (0..70; slot 32/' ' is legitimately blank, not missing). It is a distinct typeface from CoK/DoK: only 1 of the 64 addressable slots is byte-identical to Champions of Krynn's own font, versus CoK==DoK at 64/64. Now decoded and shown as a third frame card here: a 128x32 sheet of the 64 addressable slots (16 cols x 4 rows, fold/code order).

files.label: SPRIT1 (monster sprites, 3 view-sizes)
files.note: VGA compressed picture. Across sprit1..sprit6 the family is 35 blocks x 3 frames of 88x88 — the near/mid/far view-size triple. ALL 35 blocks (unlike Pools, where only 3 of 29 do) declare DAC entries 32..255 and pad the whole 32..175 range with white (63,63,63); 8.81% of non-transparent pixels index into that padded window and render white here. Unlike Pools there is no shared window anywhere in Buck's own picture data to resolve these from: its 40 non-padded pic1..pic9 blocks carry 40 pairwise-distinct full palettes (their own 32..175 ranges are 40 pairwise-distinct segments too), so no static in-file source for the missing 32..175 colours exists — compositing these sprites correctly needs a colour source outside this DAX corpus.

files.label: MARSCOM (Mars combat set)
files.note: One block holding 42 chunky items — the Buck-Rogers counterpart of the DUNGCOM/WILDCOM banks in the AD&D titles.

files.label: SHIPS (spacecraft art + stats)
files.note: 41 blocks: 35 render as art, and 6 (#40..#44, #50) are 108-byte data records, not pictures — a u8 length and a 15-byte fixed-width name buffer whose tail is never cleared (06 'Hubble' still carries 'OUT CRUIS' behind it), then little-endian u16 stats. Named ships: Hubble, Adder, Mohave, Flare, Liberator, Maelstrom Rider.

files.label: ECL1 (event scripts)
files.note: CORRECTED 2026-09-04: this note said "Buck's ECL dialect has not been verified against its own binary", which stopped being true in round 29. ECL_GEN1_BUCK was derived from Buck's OWN GAME.OVR dispatcher and operand parser (tools/map_buck_ecl_dispatch.py), with every operand count read from its handler's own prefetch rather than fitted to make the corpus decode. Under it, 23 of these 25 blocks reach a clean terminating EXIT and 2 desync (ecl1#18@0x395, ecl6#99@0x2c0), both explicitly unattributed. That clean-EXIT count is a LOWER BOUND: it stops at each block's first EXIT, and round 33's all-entry-point walk finds 195 deep desync sites across the same 25 blocks (packages/engine/test/eclReachability.test.ts). Still true: no Buck route is claimed in the campaign matrix and no gameplay route executes these blocks -- this row is an asset listing, not a playability claim.

files.label: MON0CHA (monster tables)
files.note: 54 blocks. Buck numbers its monster tables from 0, not 1.

files.label: MUSIC (music banks)
files.note: 9 blocks: block 1 is the driver, blocks 2-9 are 8 GLBR song blocks, decoded by the same already-shipped GLBR reader that DoK/Gateway/Treasures/Pools of Darkness use, with zero code changes. The dashboard now reports a census straight from this file: 8 songs, 1959 note/rest/control events, 31 channel streams. This is a decode/census result, not a confirmed-playback claim -- a byte scan of this title's own driver blob found no AdLib/CMS hardware port-write immediate anywhere, unlike the other four GLBR titles, so real hardware playback through this driver is unconfirmed even though the song data decodes cleanly (see docs/glbr-format.md).

files.label: BUCK.CFG (install config)
files.note: Five CRLF fields: display mode (V), sound (A), input (M), save path, then F and a run of zeros. Same field order as Champions' KRYNN.CFG, which holds E in the first slot.
